title: AF-4-part-2
description: Airframe exam covering flight control systems: powered and manual controls, artificial feel, spoilers, flaps/slats, stall warning and protection, trim systems, yaw damper, and fly-by-wire/light control electronics, drawn from the AF-4 flight control systems question/answer bank.

questions.question: Which component changes hydraulic motion into rotary motion?
questions.explanation: A hydraulic motor converts fluid flow/pressure into continuous rotary mechanical motion, unlike a linear actuator which produces straight-line motion.

questions.question: The stall prevention system is prevented from activating by what input?
questions.explanation: Weight-on-wheels sensing inhibits stall protection system activation while the aircraft is on the ground, since stall warning is only relevant in flight.

questions.question: Which valve transfers fluid to a hydraulic cylinder at a pressure proportional to an electrical signal it receives (based on position/velocity)?
questions.explanation: A servo valve precisely meters hydraulic flow/pressure to an actuator in proportion to an electrical command signal, enabling accurate closed-loop control.

questions.question: Which of the following is a known limitation (problem) of a spring-type artificial feel system?
options: A. It provides no feel at any speed
B. It cannot be adjusted at all
C. It is not as effective at higher airspeeds
questions.explanation: A simple spring feel system provides a relatively constant force gradient, which doesn't properly scale with the increased aerodynamic loads felt at higher airspeeds.

questions.question: Which component controls hydraulic fluid flow in the Power Control Actuator (PCA) in response to spoiler commands?
questions.explanation: The EHSV converts the electrical spoiler command signal into a proportional hydraulic flow to drive the power control actuator.

questions.question: Which mechanism, located between the pilot's and copilot's controls, isolates the two and gives priority to the pilot's command if a jam occurs?
questions.explanation: A disconnect mechanism (such as a breakout/shear device) allows the controls to be mechanically separated if one side jams, letting the unaffected pilot retain control.

questions.question: Which type of flight control system requires an artificial feel system?
options: A. A simple manually reversible control system
B. A spring-tab assisted control system
C. A fully powered (hydraulically actuated) control system
questions.explanation: Fully powered controls remove direct aerodynamic feedback to the pilot, so an artificial feel system must simulate realistic control forces.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a counterweight on the control column?
options: B. To increase control surface travel
questions.explanation: A mass-balance counterweight on the control column helps dampen unwanted oscillatory motion, reducing the tendency for pilot-induced oscillation.

questions.question: Which device is located between the system (normal) hydraulic pressure and the hand pump in a flight control system?
options: C. A cylinder/throttle (check or selector) valve
questions.explanation: A throttle/check valve arrangement isolates the hand pump circuit from normal system pressure, preventing backflow or cross-feed between the two sources.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the stick shaker?
options: A. To vibrate the control column, warning the pilot of an impending stall
B. To automatically push the nose down during a stall
C. To trim the aircraft automatically
questions.explanation: The stick shaker uses an eccentric motor to vibrate the control column, giving the pilot a strong tactile warning as the aircraft approaches a stall.

questions.question: What can cause excessive resistance to control wheel rotation?
options: A. Cable tension that is too low
B. A worn pulley bearing only
C. Cable tension that is too high
questions.explanation: Overly tight control cables increase friction throughout the system, producing noticeably higher resistance to control wheel movement.

questions.question: What is true about the stick pusher?
options: A. It only vibrates the control column
B. It pushes the control column forward when a stall identification condition is sensed
C. It only operates on the ground
questions.explanation: Unlike the stick shaker (which only warns), the stick pusher actively moves the control column forward to reduce angle of attack and help prevent an actual stall.

questions.question: How is a rudder trim tab typically actuated on large aircraft?
options: A. Only via direct pilot foot force
B. Only via engine bleed air pressure
C. Via mechanical linkage or electrical control from the cockpit trim control
questions.explanation: On large aircraft, rudder trim tabs are commonly adjusted through mechanical linkages driven by an electric trim actuator, controlled from the cockpit.

questions.question: If the rudder pedals exhibit high resistance to movement, what is a likely cause?
options: A. The rudder trim tab is disconnected
B. The rudder pedal linkage/system requires lubrication
C. The yaw damper has failed
questions.explanation: Dry or worn linkage components in the rudder pedal system commonly cause stiff, high-resistance pedal movement, often resolved by proper lubrication.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about spring-type artificial feel?
options: A. That the feel force is constant throughout the airspeed range
B. That it uses a spring to generate resistance to control input
C. That it is a relatively simple mechanical system
questions.explanation: A basic spring feel system produces a force that does not vary properly with airspeed; it does not provide a speed-appropriate (increasing) feel, contrary to this statement.

questions.question: Which component converts the pilot's manual control input into an analog electrical signal and sends it to the ACE (Actuator Control Electronics)?
questions.explanation: Force and position transducers on the pilot's controls sense control input and convert it into an analog electrical signal for processing by the ACE.

questions.question: If there is lost (free) motion between the control wheel and the control surface, what is a likely cause?
options: A. Cable tension that is too low
B. Cable tension that is too high
C. A damaged hydraulic actuator seal
questions.explanation: Slack, under-tensioned cables allow play (lost motion) between the cockpit control and the connected surface before the cable takes up and transmits movement.

questions.question: What mechanism does an aircraft use to reduce the risk of overstressing a control surface through excessive, abrupt control movement at high speed?
questions.explanation: Artificial feel devices increase the force required to move controls as airspeed increases, discouraging abrupt large inputs that could overstress the structure.

questions.question: Which component in the spoiler control system can be commanded by the spoiler control module?
questions.explanation: The spoiler control module sends commands to the power control actuators, which physically raise or lower the spoiler panels.

questions.question: What should be inspected while rigging the flap system?
options: A. The differential movement of the flap relative to the control lever position
B. Only the paint finish of the flap
questions.explanation: Flap rigging checks that flap surface position correctly corresponds (differentially, as applicable) to the cockpit control lever position throughout its range.

questions.question: Where are primary control surface travel stops typically located?
options: B. Only on the autopilot computer
C. On the control surface (or its mechanism) itself
questions.explanation: Primary stops are built into the control surface mechanism to physically limit its range of travel to the designed maximum deflection.

questions.question: What is the typical flap/slat position during the landing phase?
questions.explanation: Flaps and slats are extended to their maximum (landing) position during approach and landing to maximize lift and allow a lower approach speed.

questions.question: During operation of the stall protection system, what do the stall sensors take into account?
options: A. The color of the cockpit warning lights
B. The position of the flaps and slats
questions.explanation: Stall warning angle-of-attack thresholds are adjusted based on flap/slat configuration, since the stall angle changes with high-lift device position.

questions.question: What is used to remove induced loads from the control stick (counteracting its own weight/inertia)?
questions.explanation: A counterweight positioned to offset the control stick's own mass helps prevent unwanted induced forces or oscillations from affecting pilot feel.

questions.question: What raises and lowers the spoilers?
questions.explanation: Power control actuators (PCAs), commanded by the spoiler control system, physically move the spoiler panels up and down.

questions.question: In a hydromechanical flight control system, which of the following components belongs to the hydraulic (rather than mechanical) part?
questions.explanation: The servo valve is part of the hydraulic power circuit, converting a mechanical or electrical input into controlled hydraulic flow, unlike purely mechanical linkage components.

questions.question: A Mach trim activity light on the pilot's instrument panel flashing intermittently indicates what?
options: A. That the autopilot has disconnected
B. That the yaw damper has failed
C. That a trimming demand currently exists
questions.explanation: The Mach trim light flashes to show the system is actively commanding a trim change to compensate for Mach-related pitch trim shifts.

questions.question: What disables (inhibits) the stall warning system while the aircraft is on the ground?
questions.explanation: The landing gear squat switch senses ground contact and inhibits stall warning activation, since stall protection is only relevant in flight.

questions.question: Which flight control system component is used to detect actuator movement?
questions.explanation: Position sensors (transducers) detect and report actuator movement/position for feedback to the control system.

questions.question: What happens when both the spoiler (speed brake) lever and the brake lever conditions are in the "up/applied" position on landing?
options: A. Only the flight spoilers deploy
B. Only the ground spoilers deploy
C. Both the flight spoilers and ground spoilers deploy (are up)
questions.explanation: On landing rollout, both flight spoilers (already deployed) and ground spoilers (triggered by wheel spin-up/brake application) extend together to kill lift and aid braking.

questions.question: By what mechanism are slats typically operated on a transport aircraft?
options: A. Via mechanical linkage to a hydraulic Power Control Unit (PCU)
B. Via direct pilot cable pull with no hydraulics
questions.explanation: Slats are commonly driven by a hydraulic PCU connected through mechanical linkages (torque tubes, drive mechanisms) to each slat panel.

questions.question: What automatic flight control function counteracts the rolling and yawing motion produced by Dutch roll?
questions.explanation: The yaw damper senses and automatically counters the oscillatory yaw-roll coupling characteristic of Dutch roll, improving ride quality and stability.

questions.question: In a mechanical artificial feel system, the amount of feel force is determined by what?
options: A. The color of the control cables
B. The relative position of a fulcrum (lever ratio)
questions.explanation: Mechanical feel systems often use a movable fulcrum or linkage ratio, adjusted (e.g., by airspeed) to vary the mechanical advantage and resulting feel force.

questions.question: During a roll, the down-going wing's spoiler position is typically what?
options: B. Up (deployed, to reduce lift on that wing and assist the roll)
questions.explanation: On the down-going wing, spoilers can deploy upward to reduce lift and drag-assist the roll, complementing aileron deflection.

questions.question: What type of signal is sent from the position and force transducers to the ACE (Actuator Control Electronics)?
questions.explanation: Position and force transducers typically output an analog electrical signal representing the pilot's input, which the ACE then processes (and may digitize) for the flight control computers.

questions.question: Which unit initiates a warning or control column movement during stall detection?
questions.explanation: The Stall Warning Computer processes angle-of-attack and configuration data to trigger stick shaker and/or stick pusher activation when a stall condition is detected.

questions.question: What device converts control wheel motion into an electrical signal?
options: B. An RVDT (Rotary Variable Differential Transformer)
questions.explanation: An RVDT senses the rotational (angular) movement of the control wheel and converts it into a proportional electrical signal for the flight control system.

questions.question: Which unit interfaces with the pilot's control transducers and controls primary flight control system actuation?
options: A. The Primary Flight Computer (PFC) output stage only
questions.explanation: The ACE receives transducer signals representing pilot input and converts/relays them to drive the primary flight control actuators.

questions.question: A jumpy or binding feel in the elevator controls is often caused by what?
questions.explanation: Worn or loose hinges on the elevator can introduce binding or jumpy feel as the control surface moves unevenly through its hinge line.

questions.question: What happens to the Mach trim function if the aircraft altitude is below approximately 9,000 feet?
options: A. The system operates at double sensitivity
B. The system switches to manual-only mode
questions.explanation: Mach trim compensation is only relevant at higher altitudes/Mach numbers; below a certain altitude threshold (such as ~9,000 ft), the function is deactivated.

questions.question: The spoiler control module passes its commands to which component?
questions.explanation: Spoiler control modules send their output commands directly to the power control actuators that move the spoiler surfaces.

questions.question: What function reduces structural load from wind gusts/bending by actively adjusting control surfaces during maneuvering?
questions.explanation: Active load control/alleviation systems actively deflect ailerons or spoilers to redistribute aerodynamic load and reduce wing bending during maneuvers or gusts.

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of fly-by-cable (conventional cable-based) systems?
options: A. They require adjustment to compensate for temperature-related cable expansion/contraction
B. They cannot transmit any pilot input
C. They are immune to all wear
questions.explanation: Cable-based control systems are affected by thermal expansion and contraction, requiring rigging adjustments (such as tension regulators) to compensate.

questions.question: What is an advantage of fly-by-light over fly-by-wire and fly-by-cable systems?
options: B. No need for any sensors
C. High immunity to electromagnetic interference/lightning effects
questions.explanation: Fiber-optic (fly-by-light) signal transmission is inherently immune to electromagnetic interference and lightning-induced effects that can affect electrical wiring.

questions.question: Dutch roll is an aircraft motion consisting of an out-of-phase combination of what two motions?
questions.explanation: Dutch roll is a coupled oscillation combining yawing and rolling motion that occurs out of phase with each other, often damped by a yaw damper system.

questions.question: What is a pogo rod?
options: A. A rigid, non-flexing linkage rod
B. A spring rod that can extend or shorten when force is applied
questions.explanation: A pogo rod incorporates a spring element, allowing it to extend or compress under load, used in certain control linkage or feel system applications.

questions.question: Spoiler control modules receive the command signal and command which component to raise the spoilers?
questions.explanation: Once the spoiler control module processes the command, it directs the power control actuators to physically raise (deploy) the spoiler panels.

questions.question: What function monitors the position of flaps, slats, and Krueger flaps and delays the initiation of stall warning accordingly?
options: A. Modulation (of the stall warning angle-of-attack threshold)
questions.explanation: The stall warning system modulates (adjusts) its triggering angle of attack based on high-lift device position, since the stall angle changes with configuration.

questions.question: During high-speed flight, which spoilers are typically extended for speed brake use?
options: C. All spoilers, inboard and outboard, fully
questions.explanation: At high speed, only the inboard spoiler panels are typically used for speed braking, since deploying outboard panels at high speed could cause excessive structural loads or control issues.

questions.question: What is done to correct incorrect aileron travel?
options: B. Adjust the rudder trim tab
questions.explanation: Aileron travel is corrected by adjusting the length/position of the linkage control rods connecting the cockpit controls to the aileron mechanism.

questions.question: What is done to correct incorrect rudder travel?
options: B. Adjust the elevator trim tab
C. Adjust the bell crank stops or cable tension
questions.explanation: Rudder travel errors are corrected by adjusting the bell crank travel stops and/or the cable tension in the rudder control system.

questions.question: What is an electrically driven, out-of-balance rotor that shakes the control column when a stall warning condition is detected?
questions.explanation: The stick shaker uses an eccentric (out-of-balance) rotating mass driven by an electric motor to vibrate the control column as a tactile stall warning.

questions.question: When the speed brake lever is moved up (armed/deployed), what happens?
options: A. It retracts the landing gear
C. It moves the flight spoilers up
questions.explanation: Raising the speed brake lever commands the flight spoiler panels to deploy upward, increasing drag and reducing lift.

questions.question: What is true about spoilers?
options: A. Spoilers are only used on the ground
B. Flight spoilers are used in flight (for roll assistance and speed braking)
C. Spoilers cannot be used during flight at all
questions.explanation: Flight spoilers can be used in flight both to assist roll control and as speed brakes, in addition to ground spoiler functions during landing rollout.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT provided by the stall protection system during the various phases of approach to a stall?
questions.explanation: Stall protection systems typically provide warning (stick shaker) and, if needed, recovery assistance (stick pusher); "modal suppression" is not a standard stall protection function.

questions.question: What kind of signal is transmitted from the Actuator Control Electronics (ACE) to the Primary Flight Computer (PFC)?
questions.explanation: The ACE converts the analog transducer inputs into a digital signal format for transmission to and processing by the Primary Flight Computers.

questions.question: Spoilers are secondary control surfaces used to do what?
options: A. Increase the camber of the wing
C. Reduce the lift on a wing
questions.explanation: Spoilers disrupt (spoil) airflow over the wing, reducing lift, which is used for roll assistance, speed braking, and ground lift dumping.

questions.question: What is the role of the Primary Flight Computer (PFC)?
options: A. To store maintenance logbook entries
B. To control the cabin pressurization system
C. To calculate control surface commands using pilot input (and other data)
questions.explanation: The PFC processes pilot control inputs along with aircraft state data to calculate and issue the appropriate control surface deflection commands.

questions.question: The leading edge device surfaces are fully retracted during what flight phase, and extended during what phase to increase lift?
options: A. Retracted during takeoff, extended during cruise
B. Retracted during cruise, extended during takeoff (and landing)
C. Retracted during landing, extended during cruise
questions.explanation: Leading edge devices (slats) are retracted for low-drag cruise flight and extended during takeoff and landing to increase lift at lower speeds.

questions.question: When is the brake pedal used as a rudder pedal (in terms of its pivot/sequence)?
options: A. Only when the parking brake is set
B. When pressed from the bottom in sequence (the lower portion acts as the rudder pedal, pressed first/primarily for rudder input)
C. Only during taxi above 50 mph
questions.explanation: The rudder pedal assembly is designed so that pressing the pedal (bottom portion) provides rudder input, while pressing further forward at the top applies the wheel brakes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of trim tabs?
options: A. To increase control surface weight
B. To provide emergency hydraulic power
C. To reduce the manual control force (power/effort) required by the pilot
questions.explanation: Trim tabs aerodynamically offset the hinge moment of the primary control surface, relieving the pilot of continuously held control force in steady flight.

questions.question: Which condition could cause a configuration warning (horn/light)?
options: A. The aircraft being in cruise flight with autopilot engaged
B. The aircraft being on the ground with an unsafe takeoff configuration (e.g., flaps/trim/gear not set correctly)
C. The aircraft being fully fueled
questions.explanation: Configuration warning systems alert the crew (typically while on the ground, during the takeoff roll) if flaps, trim, or other settings are not properly configured for takeoff.

questions.question: What is the purpose of artificial feel in a powered flight control system?
options: A. To reduce the weight of the control system
B. To eliminate the need for any hydraulic power
C. To provide the pilot with a natural, speed-appropriate resistance to control input
questions.explanation: Artificial feel systems simulate the natural aerodynamic resistance a pilot would otherwise feel through unboosted controls, which is lost in a fully powered system.

questions.question: What is the difference between power-assisted and fully powered flight control systems?
options: A. In a power-assisted system, the pilot feels no forces at all
B. In a power-assisted system, the pilot still feels some actual aerodynamic forces directly through the controls
C. Fully powered systems always use artificial feel while power-assisted systems never do
questions.explanation: Power-assisted systems blend hydraulic boost with some direct aerodynamic feedback reaching the pilot, whereas fully powered systems isolate the pilot entirely, requiring artificial feel.

questions.question: What is the purpose of aileron back-drive actuators?
options: A. To synchronize the control wheel position with autopilot commands
B. To provide primary hydraulic power to the ailerons
C. To warn of an approaching stall
questions.explanation: Back-drive actuators move the cockpit control wheel to match autopilot-commanded aileron movement, so the control wheel visually/physically tracks what the autopilot is doing.

questions.question: Which component changes the control command signals to digital format and sends them to the Primary Flight Computers (PFCs)?
questions.explanation: The ACE processes the raw analog transducer signals and converts them into digital format before relaying the commands to the PFCs.

questions.question: If the rudder pedals do not hold their neutral position when the rudder is streamlined, what is the needed corrective action?
options: A. Replace the rudder trim tab
questions.explanation: A rudder pedal that doesn't settle to neutral when the rudder is centered typically indicates a rigging error, corrected by re-rigging the rudder cable system.

questions.question: During inspection and troubleshooting of the rudder control system, what is a probable cause of excessive resistance to rudder pedal movement?
options: A. Cable tension that is too low
B. Cable tension that is too high
C. A disconnected rudder trim actuator
questions.explanation: Overly tight rudder cables increase friction throughout the linkage, producing noticeably stiffer, harder-to-move rudder pedals.

questions.question: During inspection of the aileron system, what is a probable cause of lost motion between the control wheel and the aileron?
options: A. Cable tension that is too low
B. Cable tension that is too high
C. A worn stick shaker motor
questions.explanation: Slack (low-tension) aileron cables allow free play between the control wheel and the aileron surface before the cable takes up and transmits motion.

questions.question: What is the effect if the aileron bell crank stops are not properly adjusted?
options: A. Incorrect aileron travel (too much or too little deflection)
B. No effect on aileron operation
C. Automatic correction by the yaw damper
questions.explanation: Bell crank stops define the mechanical limits of aileron travel; if misadjusted, the aileron will deflect more or less than its designed range.

questions.question: Which type of stall warning system is commonly used on light aircraft?
options: A. A full digital fly-by-wire stall protection computer
B. A pneumatic (reed horn) stall warning system
C. A radar-based stall detection system
questions.explanation: Many light aircraft use a simple pneumatic stall warning device, where airflow over a wing-mounted sensor activates a horn as the stall angle is approached.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the functions performed by the stall protection system?
questions.explanation: Spoiler operation is handled by the separate spoiler control system, not by the stall protection system, which focuses on stall warning and recovery assistance (shaker/pusher).
